claim: DreamCoder-style wake/abstract/dream loop lifts held-out solve rate and cuts search time in domains with shared structure and a verifier (text editing 3.7% to 79.6% in 10 min; LOGO and towers near 100% vs under 60% for alternatives).
agent_test: Run subgoal-library loop vs no-library at equal tokens on a held-out task set with a checker. All numbers come from one paper (Ellis 2021); LAPS and LILO reuse the system, they are not independent replications.

claim: Both sleep phases matter in DreamCoder: removing library growth or the recognition net lowers held-out solves; storing whole solutions (memorise) is worse than compressing.
agent_test: Ablate abstraction vs retrieval-prompt (dream analogue) vs raw-solution memory at equal tokens.

claim: Library depth correlates with tasks solved (r = 0.79); learned routines build on each other (filter, max, nth largest, sort).
agent_test: Track library depth vs held-out solve rate across cycles.

claim: DreamCoder is compute-heavy: about a day on 20-100 CPUs per domain, about 5 days on 64 CPUs for the Lisp bootstrap.
agent_test: Cost accounting: count wake and sleep tokens, not just test tokens.

claim: Top-down compression (Stitch) replaces DreamCoder's refactoring step with 3-4 orders of magnitude less time and 2 orders less memory at equal or better compression.
agent_test: Use cheap corpus-level pattern mining for the abstraction step.

claim: Adding language descriptions to the wake-sleep loop raises held-out solves (strings 33.4% to 52-57%; graphics best run 49.55% to 98.19%; scenes ~68% to 95.6%).
agent_test: Store a natural-language name and docstring with each subgoal; compare with unnamed entries.

claim: In LLM-driven loops, unnamed compressed abstractions hurt (LILO: -30.60 REGEX, -2.91 CLEVR, -11.11 LOGO vs plain LLM); LLM-written names and docs recover part (+9.73, +2.27, 0).
agent_test: Ablate documentation of library entries at equal tokens.

claim: LILO beats DreamCoder and the plain LLM solver on LOGO (48.95 vs 28.53 vs 32.13 mean test solve) and is roughly equal on REGEX and CLEVR vs the LLM solver (77.07 vs 76.13; 96.76 vs 88.67).
agent_test: Compare library+LLM vs LLM alone, 3+ seeds; the REGEX gain is small, so test variance.

claim: Only about 19% (998 of 5250) of abstractions an LLM proposed itself were valid; symbolic compression is more reliable than asking the LLM to abstract. A second lab-family result agrees on direction: in ASI only 15.6% of induction turns passed execution verification, and verified skills beat unverified ones by 4.2 points (d01, d02).
agent_test: Verify every proposed subgoal by execution or re-solving before it enters the library.

claim: Execution-verified LLM refactoring into helper functions (ReGAL) improves weaker open models (CodeLlama-13B LOGO 45.6 to 57.1, Date 42.8 to 68.9 (test), TextCraft 18.8 to 26.9); gains are smaller for GPT-3.5 and under distribution shift.
agent_test: Verify-then-keep gate on library items; test on a strong and a weak model.

claim: ReGAL components each matter on dev (CodeLlama-13B). Full / no curriculum: LOGO 55.0 / 36.3, Date 77.0 / 56.6, TextCraft 34.12 / 28.78; no retry 48.3, 51.9, 30.43; no prune 52.0, 65.5, 25.26; no edit 53.3, 69.6, 27.35. Curriculum is the largest effect on LOGO and Date and the smallest on TextCraft.
agent_test: Order library-building problems short to long; add retry and pruning.

claim: Voyager's growing verified skill library plus curriculum gives large gains in Minecraft (3.3x items, tech-tree milestones 6.4-15.3x faster); a random curriculum cuts items by 93%; without the library progress plateaus.
agent_test: Skill library with self-verification on a sequential task stream; ablate curriculum.

claim: In LLM library learners on math and theorem proving, learned functions are almost never reused (TroVE: 3 successful reuses in 3,201 MATH questions; LEGO-Prover: one reuse in 20,000+ lemmas) and a no-library ablation matches or beats them; gains come from sampling and self-correction. The same pattern appears elsewhere: in Dynamic Cheatsheet the empty-memory arm with the same instructions gets about half of Claude's AIME 2024 gain (d05); in LILO the matched no-library solver with search is within 0.5 points on REGEX and CLEVR (d19); frontier agents' self-written skill packs fall 8 to 11.5 points below no skills (d09).
agent_test: Always run a no-library arm with the same sample count; log reuse counts. One audit paper; the six rows read the same source.

claim: Agent Workflow Memory raises WebArena success by 12.0 points absolute (51.1% relative), but offering workflows as callable actions barely helps (+1.3 step success; called in 18.5% of tasks).
agent_test: Inject retrieved workflows as context rather than actions; measure call rate.

claim: Experience-memory systems without weight updates (Dynamic Cheatsheet, ExpeL, ReasoningBank) raise accuracy at test time, strongly where reusable code or strategy exists (Game of 24 10% to 99%; AIME 2024 23% to 50%) and little elsewhere (Claude Game of 24 12% to 14%).
agent_test: Cheatsheet memory vs none at equal tokens; count memory text in the budget.

claim: Thinking offline before the query (sleep-time compute) gives less test-time compute at equal accuracy (abstract-level factor; the body text confirms only the figures below), up to +13% (GSM) and +18% (AIME) with more sleep compute, 2.5x lower cost per query when shared across 10 queries (cost weight t = 10 for test-time tokens). Benefit grows with query predictability (log-probability bins), and in the agentic SWE-Features task it reverses at high test-time budgets.
agent_test: Precompute notes on the context before the question; count sleep tokens in the total budget.

claim: Alternating search with fine-tuning on hindsight-relabelled attempts (SOAR) lifts ARC-test (7B 14.25% to 36.25%; 72B 25.62% to 44.87%) and search alone plateaus after about 5.2k attempts. It needs weight updates, so is not directly usable in a no-training scaffold.
agent_test: Only the hindsight-relabelling idea transfers: store a failed attempt as a solution to the problem it actually solved.

claim: Generative replay prevents forgetting in continual learning (MNIST 98.5-98.8% over 5 solvers; split MNIST Class-IL 90.79 vs 19.90 none vs 20.01 EWC); regularisation fails when task identity is unknown.
agent_test: Weights-only result; background only (our agent has no weights to forget).

claim: LLM self-written rehearsal data nearly matches real-data replay in LLM continual fine-tuning (SSR 63.23 vs 10% real replay 61.49, none 17.33, upper bound 64.69).
agent_test: Weights-only; not applicable to a scaffold.

claim: Prioritised experience replay beats uniform replay (41 of 49 Atari games; DQN median 48% to 106%).
agent_test: Prioritise which stored subgoal solutions are rehearsed or retrieved by surprise or failure.

claim: Wake-sleep variants: the original algorithm optimises a wrong-direction KL; reweighted wake-sleep with more samples gives better estimates but can stick in local optima where model support is never widened.
agent_test: Background; analogue: dreams made from the library alone can never widen the library's reach.

claim: Cross-paper pattern: library and memory loops help when tasks share structure, a verifier exists and entries get reused; they are null where reuse is rare.
agent_test: Per-task reuse rate as a gating predictor: measure whether it predicts gain.

claim: Execution-verified skills in memory beat unverified ones, and entry format matters by use: in WebArena shopping (Claude) unverified text 32.6, verified program 36.4, verified text 39.0 as memory; verified program as callable action 40.1. ASI beats AWM 40.4 vs 36.3 overall with 10.6% fewer steps.
agent_test: Store entries as short text in the prompt; verify by re-solving before keeping. Check the verified-text vs unverified-text gap in our own tasks.

claim: Storing failures helps only when written as abstract lessons: ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7 with failures added; AWM 44.4 to 42.2 and Synapse 40.6 to 41.7 with raw routines. No test compares this to SOAR-style hindsight relabelling.
agent_test: Write each failed attempt as one lesson (what was tried, why it failed, what to do instead); do not store raw failed traces.

claim: The number of memory items injected must stay small: ReasoningBank best at the smallest setting (49.7), falling to 45.5 with 3 and 44.4 with 4; Memento (case bank, similarity retrieval) peaks at K=4 (F1 64.5) and plateaus to K=32 (63.9).
agent_test: Inject at most 1 to 4 library entries per step; test 1, 2, 4, 8 on our tasks.

claim: In-prompt skill selection from a flat list breaks at modest size: above 90% accuracy at 20 skills or fewer, about 20% at 200; near-duplicate skills are the main cause, and two-stage routing restored 45 to 83-85% (GPT-4o-mini) and 63 to 72% (GPT-4o) at 120 skills. Single-author preprint, synthetic.
agent_test: Cap flat libraries at a few dozen entries; merge near-duplicates in the sleep step; route by group first.

claim: Self-written skills are not enough: SkillsBench v4 self-generated skill packs scored 8.1 to 11.5 points below no skills for three frontier agent configurations, while curated skills added 18 to 25 points. Focused 1 to 3 skill packs and compact length beat larger or exhaustive packs (comprehensive +0.7 pp).
agent_test: Do not let the agent write a whole library in one pass before the task; use verified, short, task-triggered entries.

claim: A no-weights practice loop (propose a skill, execute, LLM-judge, unit-test, keep as API) lifted web agents: WebArena +31.8% relative, live sites +39.8% relative (40.2 to 56.2), with 0% on one site (Car, 9 tasks). No equal-token no-practice control exists.
agent_test: Dreaming analogue to test: generate practice variants from a library entry, solve, keep only those that pass a check.

claim: LLM-written memory should be edited by small itemised updates, not full rewrites: full rewrite collapsed an 18,282-token context to 122 tokens with accuracy 66.7 to 57.1 (below the 63.7 baseline); itemised updates cut adaptation latency 82-92% and gave +10.6% on agents, and worked without labels (+14.8%).
agent_test: Update the library by add, edit or remove single items; never let one call rewrite the whole library.

claim: Gaps 2, 4 and 5 stay open: no paper reports tokens saved per library reuse (build cost known: about 0.8M-1.2M tokens per LILO iteration), no unrelated lab replicated DreamCoder-style gains on open-ended reasoning, and no verifier for non-code reasoning steps was found.
agent_test: Run our own break-even: log tokens per wake and sleep cycle and per reuse; test a verifier based on re-solving.
